mappings.note: Hydroponics bypassing soil by feeding roots from nutrient solution. Same code as the earlier hydroponics MCQ: cited to LO-3 as a land-and-water-efficient method, because the frame has no LO for agricultural technology and C-SST1.1-LO-1 is for identifying soils, not for dispensing with one.

State procurement of staple crops so farmers can market produce at fair prices. Goal-level CG-SST4, which names market and government together; C-SST4.2-LO-1 is rejected because that LO is a field visit to a local market or shopping complex, not the procurement system.
Shrinking holdings averaging three-quarters of a hectare and the ceiling this puts on earnings. Goal-level CG-SST4; no LO covers landholding.

Climate change threatening agriculture through unpredictable weather and extreme drought. LO-1 explicitly names drought; C-SST1.2-LO-2 is rejected here because the question is about the hazard, not about the normal climate of a region.

Why Himalayan glaciers melt at unprecedented rates, answered as global warming. The frame has no climate-change LO; LO-2 is the nearest for the atmospheric driver and LO-3 for the loss of the water source the glaciers are. Flagged as a partial frame gap.

Long answer on women's role: over 75 percent of the rural farm workforce doing most daily operations. C-SST4.1-LO-1 for the unrecognised labour that the chapter frames as a disadvantage, plus CG-SST4 for the goal's clause on recognising the contributions of different sections of society.
